items.title: Beyond Direct Sight: Inferring the Momentary Arising-and-Ceasing Beneath Every Visible Change

items.zh: 即由如是現見增上作意力故，觀察變異無常性已。彼諸色行雖復現有剎那生滅、滅壞無常，而微細故，非現所得。故依現見增上作意，應正比度。
items.en: Through this very power of mental engagement resting on direct observation, having already observed the impermanent nature of change, these very physical processes, although they genuinely possess momentary arising and ceasing — an impermanence of destruction — are, because so subtle, not something direct observation itself can grasp. So, resting still on that same power of mental engagement built on direct observation, one should correctly infer it instead.

items.zh: 謂彼諸行，要有剎那生滅滅壞，方可得有前後變異，非如是住得有變異。是故諸行必定應有剎那生滅。彼彼眾緣和合有故，如是如是諸行得生，生已不待滅壞因緣，自然滅壞。
items.en: These processes must have momentary arising, ceasing, and destruction — only then can there be any prior-and-later change to observe at all; they could not show such change while simply persisting unchanged … because this or that gathering of conditions comes together, these or those processes are able to arise; and having arisen, without needing to wait for any further destroying condition, they cease of themselves.

items.title: Section: Fire Never Truly Destroys Anything — It Only Changes What's There

items.zh: 如是所有變異因緣，能令諸行轉變生起。此是變異生起因緣，非是諸行滅壞因緣。所以者何？由彼諸行，與世現見滅壞因緣俱滅壞已，後不相似生起可得，非彼一切全不生起。
items.en: All these causes and conditions of change are able to bring about the arising of a transformed process — this is a cause and condition for change to arise, not a cause and condition for a process's actual destruction … these processes, together with what the world directly observes as a "destroying" condition, cease together, yet a dissimilar successor is found to arise afterwards — it is not the case that nothing whatsoever arises.

items.zh: 或有諸行既滅壞已，一切生起全不可得。如煎水等，最後一切皆悉消盡；災火焚燒器世間已，都無灰燼，乃至餘影亦不可得。彼亦因緣後後展轉漸減盡故，最後一切都無所有。不由其火作如是事。
items.en: Or else, some processes, once destroyed, yield no further arising to be found at all — as when water is boiled away until every last trace is gone, or when the great conflagration burns the physical world until not even ash remains, let alone any trace or shadow. This too comes from cause and condition diminishing further and further in succession, until in the end nothing whatsoever is left — it is not that the fire itself simply performs this act of erasure.

items.zh: 是故變異，由前所說八種因緣，令變生起，自然滅壞。如是比度作意力故，由滅壞行，於彼諸行剎那生滅、滅壞無常而得決定。於如是事得決定已，復於他世非所現見諸行生起，應正比度。云何比度？

items.title: Section: Refuting a Creator God — Why Present Differences Prove Only Past Karma

items.zh: 謂諸有情現有種種差別可得。或好形色、或惡形色，或上族姓、或下族姓、或富族姓、或貧族姓，或大宗葉、或小宗葉，或長壽命、或短壽命，言或威肅、或不威肅，或性利根、或性鈍根。如是一切有情差別，定由作業有其差別，方可成立，非無作業。如是有情色類差別，定由先世善不善業造作增長種種品類。
items.en: One observes that beings display all manner of differences: fine form or coarse form, high lineage or low, wealth or poverty, large clan or small, long life or short, commanding speech or not, sharp faculties or dull … all such differences among beings can only be established as arising definitely from differences in past action — never from the absence of action. Such differences among the various kinds of beings definitely arise from wholesome or unwholesome karma accumulated and increased in former lives.

items.zh: 由彼因緣，於今自體差別生起，不應自在變化為因。何以故？
若說自在變化為因，能生諸行，此所生行為唯用彼自在為緣？為待餘緣，如是自在方能變化。若唯用彼自在為緣，是則諸行與彼自在俱應本有，何須更生。若言先有自在體性，然後行生，是則諸行不唯自在為緣生起。
items.en: If one claims that a sovereign deity, as sole cause, is able to produce these processes — are the processes thus produced brought about by that deity as the only condition, or must some further condition be present before that deity is even able to bring about the transformation? If the deity alone is the condition, then these processes and that deity ought both to have existed from the very beginning — what need is there for anything to be produced at all? And if one says the deity's own nature exists first, and only afterwards do the processes arise, then the processes are plainly not produced by that deity as their sole condition after all.

items.zh: 若言自在隨其所欲、功用、祈願，方能造化，是故亦用欲為因緣，非唯自在。若爾，此欲為有因耶？為無因耶？若言有因，即用自在以為因者，此則同前所說過失，不應道理。若言此欲更有餘因，是則如欲，功用、祈願離自在外，餘法為因。如是亦應一切諸行皆用餘法以為其因，何須妄計無用自在。由如是等比度增上作意力故，於有他世諸行生起獲得決定。

items.title: Three Kinds of Strengthened Attention, and Separation as Impermanence's Third Aspect

items.zh: 如是略由三種增上作意力故，尋思觀察內外諸行是無常性。謂淨信增上作意力故，現見增上作意力故，比度增上作意力故。
items.en: Thus, in brief, by means of three kinds of strengthened mental engagement, one investigates and observes that internal and external processes alike are impermanent by nature — namely, mental engagement strengthened by pure trust, mental engagement strengthened by direct observation, and mental engagement strengthened by inference.

items.zh: 於前所舉能隨順修無常五行，已辯變異、滅壞二行。云何復由別離行故觀無常性？謂依內外二種別離，應知諸行是無常性。依內別離無常性者，
謂如有一，先為他主，非奴、非使，能自受用，能驅役他作諸事業；彼於後時退失主性，非奴使性，轉得他奴及所使性。於主性等，名為別離無常之性。
items.en: For instance, someone who was formerly another's master — neither a servant nor one commanded by others, able to enjoy things freely and to command others to carry out various tasks — later loses that condition of mastery, and, no longer free of servitude, instead comes to take on the very condition of being a servant, commanded by others. This losing of one's former condition of mastery and the like is called the impermanence of separation.

blocks.text: From what can be seen to what must be inferred: momentary arising and ceasing. Then an argument against a creator. A short passage (0473c09) is untranslated.

Visible changes imply something subtler: these processes "must have momentary arising and ceasing; only then can there be any prior-and-later change to observe". They "could not show such change while simply persisting unchanged". This momentary impermanence is "so subtle, not something direct observation can grasp", so one infers it.

The causes of change "bring about the arising of a transformed process; they are causes of change, not causes of destruction". Things cease by themselves, moment by moment; fire only makes what follows different. "Even when water is boiled away until no trace is left, or the great fire burns the world until not even ash remains", it is still change. Venerable Miào Jìng: the water's form is gone, but something else continues.

Beings differ: fine or coarse, high or low, rich or poor, long-lived or short. "All such differences can only arise from differences in past karma." If a sovereign god were the sole cause, "then these processes and that god would have existed together from the beginning"; if other conditions were needed, the god is not the sole cause. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the argument.
Through scripture (pure faith), direct observation, and inference, one investigates impermanence. Then **separation**: "one who was formerly another's master later loses that condition".

quiz.q: Momentary arising and ceasing is "too subtle for direct observation." How does one know it, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: infer it with the sixth consciousness's wisdom
quiz.why: "Because so subtle, not something direct observation itself can grasp. So, resting still on that same power of mental engagement built on direct observation, one should correctly infer it instead." Master Cháng Bǎi: subtle impermanence can't be directly seen by the eye, but can be inferred by the wisdom of the sixth consciousness.

quiz.q: Causes of change "are not causes of destruction." How does Master Cháng Bǎi apply this to a house fire?
options: fire isn't the house's cause of cessation but of change
quiz.why: "This is a cause and condition for change to arise, not a cause and condition for a process's actual destruction." Master Cháng Bǎi: fire isn't the cause of the house's cessation; fire is a condition of the house's change.

quiz.q: "As when water is boiled away until every trace is gone … not the fire itself." What do the lectures add?
options: both note it really evaporates — into vapour or dust — not total nothingness
quiz.why: "As when water is boiled away until every last trace is gone." Venerable Miào Jìng: the water's form is gone, but the water has turned to vapour. Master Cháng Bǎi's lecture, relaying Venerable Miào Jìng: actually it evaporates and becomes dust.

quiz.q: "If one claims that a sovereign deity is the cause" — what deity, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: Maheśvara, whom outsiders hold transforms the world of beings
quiz.why: "If one claims that a sovereign deity, as sole cause, is able to produce these processes." Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders hold that beings' differences come from Maheśvara transforming the world of beings.

quiz.q: "Processes and the deity should both exist from the start — why be produced?" What counterexample does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: airplanes and nuclear bombs appeared only in recent years
quiz.why: "If the deity alone is the condition, then these processes and that deity ought both to have existed from the very beginning — what need is there for anything to be produced at all?" Venerable Miào Jìng: only in recent years have there been airplanes and nuclear bombs.

quiz.q: To show differences "definitely arise from action," what story about a leader does Venerable Miào Jìng tell?
quiz.why: "All such differences among beings can only be established as arising definitely from differences in past action — never from the absence of action." Venerable Miào Jìng tells of Chiang Kai-shek at Xuědòu Temple: he dreamed he was a monk.

quiz.q: Three strengthened engagements — trust, direct observation, inference. What do they do, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: through these three, one cultivates right view of impermanence
quiz.why: "Namely, mental engagement strengthened by pure trust, mental engagement strengthened by direct observation, and mental engagement strengthened by inference." Master Cháng Bǎi: through these three means of knowledge, one can cultivate right view of impermanence.
